suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-29 adds this relationship only as a bounded psychosocial-burden association. Facial acne scarring is associated with depressive symptoms and impaired quality of life in cross-sectional studies, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish a depressive disorder in every person or determine an individual's cause, severity, or course. Require independently documented acne scarring and a diagnosed depressive disorder, compatible chronology and course, objective psychiatric assessment, and mental-health review. Preserve pre-existing mood disorder, psychosocial stressors, other dermatologic or medical illness, medication effects, substance use, and other competing causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of clinically significant acne scarring and of a diagnosed depressive disorder
Structured psychiatric assessment such as PHQ-9, HADS, or clinical interview records
Chronology of scarring onset, persistence, and depressive-symptom course
Assessment of prior mood disorder, psychosocial stressors, other medical illness, medication effects, and substance use
Mental-health assessment distinguishing scar-associated mood symptoms from other depressive etiologies

sourceReferences.citation: Heah MM, Ng RS, Low DW, Mohd Ali N, Jamil A. The impact of facial acne scars on quality of life, anxiety, depression and its associated risk factors. Med J Malaysia. 2025;80(3):313-320. PMID 40437720.
sourceReferences.note: Cross-sectional study associating facial acne scar severity with anxiety, depression, and quality-of-life impairment. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 40437720; scar-severity and HADS association findings

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Depressive symptoms are reported at higher rates among people with facial acne scarring, but cross-sectional association evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both conditions, compatible chronology, structured psychiatric assessment, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Visible disfigurement can contribute to body-image distress and social withdrawal that accompany depressive symptoms, but the precise contribution and individual clinical pathway must be established from the patient's psychiatric history and objective mental-health assessment.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Acne-scar severity is associated with depressive symptoms and quality-of-life impairment in cross-sectional data, but the study does not establish that acne scarring caused or aggravated a depressive disorder in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, structured assessment, treatment, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent acne-scarring and depressive-disorder documentation; structured psychiatric testing and chronology; prior mood history, stressor, medication, and substance review; mental-health assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing or independent major depressive disorder or bipolar-spectrum illness
Psychosocial stressors, other medical illness, or medication effects including acne treatment agents
Substance use or other psychiatric comorbidity explaining depressive symptoms
